title: Contoso Bank — Grounded customer-support agent
scenario: Contoso Bank is building a customer-support chat agent that must answer questions grounded in the bank's policy library, act on behalf of customers through internal APIs, and produce consistent, measurable, and safe responses.
context: Ground answers in the bank's policy library stored in Azure AI Search.
Let the agent query customer account data through an internal API.
Keep responses consistent and factual rather than creative.
Measure answer quality before release and trace issues in production.

questions.domain: Implement generative AI and agentic solutions
questions.prompt: How should the agent ground its answers in the policy library?
options: Retrieve relevant policy chunks with Azure AI Search and inject them into the prompt (RAG)
Fine-tune the model once on all policy PDFs
Hard-code every policy into the system prompt
Store policies in Blob Storage and ignore them at runtime
questions.explanation: Retrieval-Augmented Generation pulls the most relevant documents and injects them into the prompt so answers are grounded in current data. Fine-tuning shapes style and format rather than retrieving changing knowledge, hard-coding does not scale, and ignoring the store defeats grounding.

questions.domain: Implement generative AI and agentic solutions
questions.prompt: Which capability lets the model request an account-balance lookup through the bank's internal API?
options: Raising temperature to its maximum value
questions.explanation: Function calling returns a structured request the application uses to invoke the API, then passes the result back to the model. Temperature only changes output randomness, disabling safety filters is unrelated and unsafe, and batching is not tool use.

questions.domain: Implement generative AI and agentic solutions
questions.prompt: The agent must give consistent, factual answers. Which temperature setting is most appropriate?
options: A high value, near the maximum
Leave temperature unset and rely only on top_p
questions.explanation: A low temperature makes output deterministic and focused, which suits factual support. Higher temperatures increase randomness and creativity, risking hallucinations; leaving the setting unset or relying only on top_p does not guarantee consistency.

questions.domain: Plan and manage an Azure AI solution
questions.prompt: How should the team measure answer quality and debug issues in production?
options: Run evaluations (groundedness, relevance) in Foundry and enable tracing
Deploy and ask users to report errors manually
Review the monthly Azure invoice for cost spikes
Keep prompts in a shared spreadsheet
questions.explanation: Foundry evaluation scores quality metrics against a test dataset, and tracing records each request's steps for debugging. Manual reporting does not scale, invoices do not measure quality, and spreadsheets do not trace execution.

title: Fabrikam Logistics — Document intake and redaction pipeline
scenario: Fabrikam Logistics is digitizing its shipping paperwork: scanned forms, invoices, and identification documents. It needs to extract text and structured fields, redact personal data before storage, and understand customer feedback.
context: Extract printed text from scanned shipping documents.
Pull structured fields such as invoice number and total from invoices without training.
Redact personal data (names, ID numbers) before storing documents.
Classify whether customer emails are positive or negative.

questions.prompt: Which service extracts structured fields from invoices with no model training?
options: A custom neural model trained from scratch
questions.explanation: The prebuilt invoice model returns fields such as invoice number and total out of the box. A custom neural model requires labeled training data, Azure AI Face handles faces, and sentiment analysis classifies text polarity rather than extracting document fields.

questions.prompt: How should printed text be extracted from the scanned documents?
questions.explanation: OCR/Read extracts printed or handwritten text from images and PDFs. Custom Vision detects or classifies objects rather than text, speech-to-text processes audio, and key phrase extraction summarizes existing text instead of reading images.

questions.prompt: How should Fabrikam remove names and ID numbers before storing documents?
questions.explanation: PII detection finds and can redact personal data. Sentiment and language detection classify text but do not remove data, and translation converts text between languages.

questions.prompt: How should Fabrikam determine whether customer emails are positive or negative?
questions.explanation: Sentiment analysis returns positive, negative, or neutral polarity for text. OCR reads images, the invoice model extracts invoice fields, and Custom Vision classifies images — none of them classify the opinion of text.
